attackPath.change_conditions: Path validation ensuring resolved path remains within ROOT, or allowlist of permitted filenames.
attackPath.dataflow: Attacker-controlled req.query.name flows into path.join(ROOT, name), resolving ../ segments to escape ROOT. The resolved path is passed to fs.readFile().
attackPath.impact: Read arbitrary files from the server filesystem including configuration files, source code, and secrets.
attackPath.reachability: The /file endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication. Any unauthenticated attacker can craft a request with ../ in the name parameter.
attackPath.severity_rationale: Publicly accessible route with no authentication. Can read sensitive files like /etc/passwd, application source code, or configuration files containing secrets.

codeEvidence.explanation: User-controlled name is joined with ROOT without validation, allowing ../ traversal.
codeEvidence.label: Unsafe path construction

confidence.rationale: Direct evidence: req.query.name flows into path.join(ROOT, name) without any validation or sanitization. path.join does not prevent ../ traversal from escaping ROOT. The /file endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication.

findings.remediation: Validate the resolved path to ensure it remains within ROOT. Use path.relative() to check the resolved path is a subpath of ROOT, or use an allowlist of permitted filenames. Reject requests containing ../ or other traversal sequences.

rootCause.summary: User-controlled input (req.query.name) flows directly into filesystem path construction via path.join(ROOT, name) without any validation that the resolved path remains within the intended ROOT directory.

findings.summary: The /file endpoint constructs file paths from req.query.name using path.join(ROOT, name) without validating that the resolved path remains within ROOT, allowing ../ traversal to escape the public directory and read arbitrary files from the server filesystem.
findings.title: Path traversal in /file endpoint

validation.confidence_rationale: Direct evidence of unvalidated user input flowing into filesystem operations.
validation.evidence: path.join(ROOT, name) resolves ../ segments, allowing directory traversal beyond ROOT.
validation.method: static analysis with manual verification of path resolution
validation.rubric: User-controlled input flows into a filesystem operation without validation.

attackPath.change_conditions: URL allowlisting, scheme restriction, blocking of private/internal IP ranges, or disabling user-provided URLs for server-side fetching.
attackPath.dataflow: Attacker-controlled req.query.url flows directly into http.get(url, ...) with no validation. The server issues outbound HTTP requests to arbitrary URLs.
attackPath.impact: Access internal network services, retrieve cloud instance metadata (including IAM credentials), perform port scanning, and potentially achieve account compromise.
attackPath.reachability: The /preview endpoint is publicly accessible without authentication. Any unauthenticated attacker can supply arbitrary URLs targeting internal services or cloud metadata.
attackPath.severity_rationale: Publicly accessible route with no authentication. SSRF against cloud metadata can yield IAM credentials leading to full cloud account compromise. Internal service access exposes sensitive APIs.

codeEvidence.explanation: User-controlled URL is passed directly to http.get() with no validation, allowing SSRF.
codeEvidence.label: Unvalidated URL in outbound request

confidence.rationale: Direct evidence: req.query.url is passed directly to http.get() without any URL parsing, scheme validation, or allowlist check. The server acts as an HTTP client for arbitrary URLs.

findings.remediation: Implement URL validation: parse the URL, restrict to HTTPS scheme, maintain an allowlist of permitted hostnames, and block requests to private/internal IP ranges. Alternatively, disable direct user-provided URLs.

rootCause.summary: User-controlled input (req.query.url) flows directly into an outbound HTTP request (http.get) without validation, scheme restriction, or destination allowlisting.

findings.summary: The /preview endpoint passes req.query.url directly to http.get() without URL validation, scheme checking, or destination restrictions, allowing requests to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.
findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery in /preview endpoint

validation.confidence_rationale: Direct evidence of unvalidated user input flowing into network request construction.
validation.evidence: http.get() issues requests to any URL the attacker specifies, including internal services and cloud metadata.
validation.method: static analysis of URL handling and network request construction
validation.rubric: User-controlled input flows into an outbound network request without validation.
